title: KPI Trust Ledger
subtitle: Lone Star Care Operations (fictional) · three systems report the same appeals process and none of them agree. Backlog is 423, 611, 509 or 211 depending on which extract you open. This page reconciles 6 KPIs across 3 sources and certifies only the ones that survive the test — 2 of 6.
limitations: Tolerance bands are set by judgement, not by a measurement-error model, so a KPI marked within tolerance is agreed, not proven correct. The certified value is the authoritative source's value — being certified means the sources agree, not that reality was observed. 5 of 18 KPI-source pairs are untestable because the source does not carry the field, and an untestable pair is neither a pass nor a fail. The data is fully synthetic.
footer: Source: synthetic extracts generated by src/generate_sources.py, reconciled by src/reconcile.py. No employer data, patient information, protected health information or confidential business information is used.

queries.headline: SELECT COUNT(*) AS kpis, SUM(CASE WHEN Certified='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS certified, SUM(Sources_Tested) AS pairs_tested, SUM(Sources_Within_Tolerance) AS pairs_agreed, ROUND(100.0*SUM(Sources_Within_Tolerance)/NULLIF(SUM(Sources_Tested),0),1) AS recon_rate, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM kpi_reconciliation WHERE Within_Tolerance IS NULL) AS not_testable FROM kpi_certification
queries.vol: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM reporting_layer) AS reporting_rows, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_management_export) AS cm_rows, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM workflow_tracker_export) AS wt_rows, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM leadership_reporting_extract) AS lr_rows, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dq_exceptions) AS exceptions
queries.certification: SELECT KPI_ID, KPI_Name, Certified_Value, Unit, Sources_Tested, Sources_Within_Tolerance, Certified, COALESCE(Blocking_Reason,'—') AS Blocking_Reason FROM kpi_certification ORDER BY KPI_ID
queries.cert_chart: SELECT KPI_ID AS kpi, Sources_Within_Tolerance AS agreed, Sources_Tested-Sources_Within_Tolerance AS disagreed FROM kpi_certification ORDER BY KPI_ID
queries.recon: SELECT KPI_ID, KPI_Name, CASE Source WHEN 'case_management' THEN 'Case management' WHEN 'workflow_tracker' THEN 'Workflow tracker' WHEN 'leadership_extract' THEN 'Leadership extract' ELSE Source END AS Source, Source_Value, Certified_Value, Variance, Unit, Tolerance, Within_Tolerance, COALESCE(Note,'—') AS Note FROM kpi_reconciliation ORDER BY KPI_ID, Source
queries.by_source: SELECT CASE Source WHEN 'case_management' THEN 'Case management' WHEN 'workflow_tracker' THEN 'Workflow tracker' WHEN 'leadership_extract' THEN 'Leadership extract' ELSE Source END AS Source, COUNT(*) AS pairs, SUM(CASE WHEN Within_Tolerance='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS agreed, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN Within_Tolerance='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN Within_Tolerance IN ('Yes','No') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),1) AS recon_pct FROM kpi_reconciliation GROUP BY Source ORDER BY recon_pct DESC
queries.backlog: SELECT 'Certified (reporting layer)' AS source, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM reporting_layer WHERE Closed_Date IS NULL OR Closed_Date='') AS backlog UNION ALL SELECT 'Case management export', (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_management_export WHERE Closed_Date IS NULL OR Closed_Date='') UNION ALL SELECT 'Workflow tracker', (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM workflow_tracker_export WHERE Completion_Date IS NULL OR Completion_Date='') UNION ALL SELECT 'Leadership extract', (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM leadership_reporting_extract WHERE ClosedDate IS NULL OR ClosedDate='')
queries.variance: SELECT KPI_ID||' · '||CASE Source WHEN 'case_management' THEN 'Case management' WHEN 'workflow_tracker' THEN 'Workflow tracker' WHEN 'leadership_extract' THEN 'Leadership extract' ELSE Source END AS pair, ROUND(Variance,2) AS variance, Tolerance, Within_Tolerance FROM kpi_reconciliation WHERE Within_Tolerance IN ('Yes','No') ORDER BY ABS(Variance) DESC LIMIT 13
queries.exceptions: SELECT Rule_ID, Severity, COUNT(*) AS exceptions, SUM(CASE WHEN Status='Open' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS still_open FROM dq_exceptions GROUP BY Rule_ID, Severity ORDER BY exceptions DESC
queries.severity: SELECT Severity, COUNT(*) AS exceptions FROM dq_exceptions GROUP BY Severity ORDER BY exceptions DESC
queries.catalog: SELECT KPI_ID, KPI_Name, Business_Definition, Formula, Authoritative_Source, Unit, Tolerance FROM kpi_catalog ORDER BY KPI_ID
queries.row_counts: SELECT 'Reporting layer (certified)' AS source, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM reporting_layer) AS rows_present UNION ALL SELECT 'Case management export', (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_management_export) UNION ALL SELECT 'Workflow tracker export', (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM workflow_tracker_export) UNION ALL SELECT 'Leadership reporting extract', (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM leadership_reporting_extract)
queries.monthly: SELECT substr(Received_Date,1,7) AS month, COUNT(*) AS received, SUM(CASE WHEN Closed_Date IS NULL OR Closed_Date='' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS still_open, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN SLA_Met='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN Closed_Date IS NOT NULL AND Closed_Date<>'' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0),2) AS sla_pct FROM reporting_layer GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

cards.title: The certification ledger
cards.desc: A KPI is certified only when every testable source agrees with the authoritative source inside tolerance. Four of six fail, and each carries the reason it failed rather than a footnote.

cards.title: How many sources agree, per KPI
cards.desc: Stacked to make the shape obvious: only the two fully green bars can be quoted in a leadership deck.

cards.title: One question, four answers
cards.desc: Open appeals at period end, counted natively in each system. This single chart is why the project exists — nobody was wrong, they were counting different things and calling them the same word.

cards.title: Reconciliation rate by source
cards.desc: The leadership extract agrees least often, which matters more than the others because it is the one executives see. It also carries the fewest fields, so fewer of its KPIs are even testable.

cards.title: Largest variances
cards.desc: Absolute variance between each source and the certified value, worst first. Units differ by row, so read this as a ranking of disagreement rather than a comparison of magnitudes.

cards.title: Full reconciliation detail
cards.desc: Every KPI-source pair tested, with its variance, the tolerance it was judged against and the note explaining untestable pairs.

cards.title: Row counts by source
cards.desc: Before any KPI is calculated the sources already disagree on how many appeals exist. Reconciling metrics without reconciling record counts first produces confident nonsense.

cards.title: Exceptions by severity
cards.desc: 273 exceptions across the three extracts. The single Critical one blocks a KPI on its own.

cards.title: Exceptions by rule
cards.desc: Which validation rule caught what, and how much is still open. An exception log with nothing open is usually a log nobody reads.

cards.title: Certified reporting layer over time
cards.desc: Built from the certified layer only. Bars are appeals received on the right axis; the line is SLA compliance, a KPI that is itself uncertified and therefore shown here as a shape rather than a number to quote.
